messages:
Ilan: hey everyone, day 1 question — trying to get dev env stable on WSL2 + VSCode. asdf shims sometimes ignored, gpg signing works in the shell but VSCode UI shows unsigned, and 1Password op session isn't visible to docker-compose. any quick checklist?
Rae: welcome! first, always open the project from the WSL distro ('code .' from WSL). otherwise VSCode will use Windows PATH.
Morgan: for asdf make sure you export ASDF_DIR and source asdf.sh in ~/.profile or ~/.zshrc before other PATH changes, e.g.
```bash
export ASDF_DIR="$HOME/.asdf"
export PATH="$ASDF_DIR/bin:$ASDF_DIR/shims:$PATH"
. "$ASDF_DIR/asdf.sh"
```
Ilan: did that, node versions look right now. GPG still weird: terminal commits signed, VSCode says unsigned and the passphrase prompt flashes.
Rae: run gnupg inside WSL and install pinentry-curses. add `pinentry-program /usr/bin/pinentry-curses` to ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf and `gpgconf --reload gpg-agent`. launching VSCode from WSL shell helps the UI pick it up.
Morgan: if you prefer GUI prompts under WSLg use pinentry-gtk-2 and point gpg-agent there. also set `git config --global gpg.program /usr/bin/gpg`.
Ilan: 1Password op: I eval the signin and token exists in shell, but docker-compose run from VSCode tasks doesn't get REDWOOD_API_KEY.
Rae: VSCode tasks spawn non-login shells. put `eval $(op signin --raw)` into ~/.profile or better use direnv with an .envrc that reads secrets: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op read "op://Redwood/Dev/REDWOOD_API_KEY")` then `direnv allow`. direnv is our preferred pattern.
OnboardingBot: Hi Ilan — internal guide: https://intranet/redwood/onboarding/dev-setup-wsl has step-by-step WSL, gpg-transfer, direnv+op examples, and Docker CA notes.
Ilan: awesome, thanks! if I still get stuck can someone pair on GPG/direnv?
Morgan: happy to pair tomorrow morning. ping me and we can screenshare.
Ilan: will do, much appreciated :thumbsup:
